### Question 3

```{r}
n <- 19; p <- 2;   # n observations, p variables
conf <- 0.90       # confidence level
xbar <- c(-2.3, 4.1)  # sample mean, this is the centre of the ellipsoid
S <- matrix(c(8, 1,
              1, 6), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)  #sample vcv matrix

# Eigendecomposition: axes of the ellipse point along the eigenvectors
e   <- eigen(S)
lambda <- e$values  # the larger eigenvalue (8.41) sets the long axis
evectors   <- e$vectors

print("eigenvalues")
print(lambda)
cat("\n")

print("eigenvectors")
print(evectors)
cat("\n")

# Fix signs so eigenvector 1 (D -> C) points north-east and eigenvector 2 (A -> B) points north-west
# If you don't do this then the ellipse points will not match what is expected
if (evectors[1, 1] < 0) evectors[, 1] <- -evectors[, 1]
if (evectors[1, 2] > 0) evectors[, 2] <- -evectors[, 2]

print("eigenvectors re-pointed")
print(evectors)

```

### Question 3a: Sigma unknown: Hotelling T^2 critical value

```{r}

# The formulas come from Topic 4 Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for the mean vector.
# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119135/slides/817755
# The section “Confidence region for the mean vector” says the ellipse axes point along the eigenvectors of S, with
# half-lengths = √λᵢ · √(p(n−1)/(n(n−p)) · F)
# hl = sqrt(lambda * c2); where c2 is the critical value which could be either Hotelling T^2 or chi-square

# Function to calculate the ends of the axes: mean +/- hl

ellipse_points <- function(c2) {
  hl <- sqrt(lambda * c2)
  rbind(A_southeast = xbar - hl[2] * evectors[, 2],
        B_northwest = xbar + hl[2] * evectors[, 2],
        C_northeast = xbar + hl[1] * evectors[, 1],
        D_southwest = xbar - hl[1] * evectors[, 1])
}

# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119135/slides/817755
# Confidence region for the mean vector

c2_T <- p * (n - 1) / (n * (n - p)) * qf(conf, p, n - p)
round(ellipse_points(c2_T), 4)

```

### Question 3b: Sigma known: chi-square critical value

```{r}
# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119135/slides/817753
# paragraph on "...known covariance matrix...tables of the χ2-distribution will suffice to perform the above test in the multivariate case."

ellipse_points_chi <- function(c2_chi) {
  hl <- sqrt(lambda * c2_chi)
  rbind(A_southeast = xbar - hl[2] * evectors[, 2],
        B_northwest = xbar + hl[2] * evectors[, 2],
        C_northeast = xbar + hl[1] * evectors[, 1],
        D_southwest = xbar - hl[1] * evectors[, 1])
}

c2_chi <- qchisq(conf, p) / n
round(ellipse_points_chi(c2_chi), 4)

```

### Question 3c: Projection (T^2) simultaneous intervals

```{r}
# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119135/slides/817755
# Theorem 1.7 (Simultaneous confidence ellipsoid) says that, simultaneously for all l, the interval
# contains lᵀμ with probability at least 1 − α. Taking l = (1, 0) and then l = (0, 1) gives lᵀSl = s₁₁ and s₂₂, the diagonal of S.
# So se is √(sⱼⱼ), and c2_T_sim is the p(n−1)/n(n−p)·F constant.

c2_T_sim <- p * (n - 1) / (n * (n - p)) * qf(conf, p, n - p)
se <- sqrt(diag(S))
round(cbind(Lower = xbar - sqrt(c2_T_sim) * se, Upper = xbar + sqrt(c2_T_sim) * se), 4)

```

### Question 3d: Bonferroni: t with alpha/(2p) in each tail

```{r}
# https://edstem.org/au/courses/41412/lessons/119135/slides/817755
# Equation (1.16) is the one-at-a-time interval
# The “Bonferroni Method” section says that for m simultaneous statements you set αᵢ = α/m

se_bon <- sqrt(diag(S) / n)

tb <- qt(1 - ((1 - conf) / (2 * p)), n - 1)

round(cbind(Lower = xbar - tb * se_bon, Upper = xbar + tb * se_bon), 4)

```
